findings.title: S21 unnecessarily restricts the observed backend request to same origin
findings.evidence: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:401 requires 'that successful update's actual absolute same-origin URL'. The public integration.md:5,11 requires a single local Node server on 0.0.0.0:3000 serving UI/API, but does not require the browser's API requests to use its exact origin. tests/gates/constraints/prompt.md:20 expressly rejects same-origin restrictions. The frozen workbook quality row 23 likewise says there is no same-origin requirement.
findings.counterexample: A correct app served at http://localhost:3000 sends observed Save requests to http://127.0.0.1:3000 with appropriate CORS. It still uses the required one local server and database. S21 cannot capture a same-origin successful update for that otherwise conforming app and risks an unavailable-evidence or failed outcome.
findings.fix: Capture the actual absolute local-backend URL and observed request/credential policy, without requiring same origin or inventing/rebasing an endpoint.
findings.evidence_kind: Source-derived conforming alternative; no alternate app was launched.

findings.title: Canonical helper still cannot guarantee actual restart and bounded cleanup
findings.evidence: tests/test.sh:152-159 sends TERM and polls for five seconds without requiring old-group death. Lines 160-183 launch a replacement, overwrite app.pid and accept any HTTP listener without replacement-PID liveness. tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:47 translates exit zero into 'the server was relaunched'. tests/test.sh:33-40 waits without a deadline during cleanup. S22 at functional/prompt.md:410 relies on completed restart. Frozen task and frozen template test.sh have identical SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa.
findings.counterexample: An in-memory server that ignores SIGTERM can remain the responding listener while the replacement fails to bind; the helper reports completion and may award durability without process replacement. A correct server with a slow graceful shutdown can similarly be misidentified, and an uncooperative child can stall cleanup.
findings.fix: Keep the shared script unchanged for this task-local repair and retain the inherited blocker pending a canonical owner-approved fix that bounds shutdown/cleanup and verifies old-group death, new-PID liveness and listener replacement.
findings.evidence_kind: Unchanged source control-flow witness; no resistant-process, cleanup or full-verifier run was performed in this review.

positive_observations.verdict_scope: Bounded protocol design improvements, subject to the same-origin finding and stated limits
positive_observations.evidence: functional/prompt.md:401-403 now allocates a dedicated monitor and carrier, establishes a successful monitor update/readback, captures current revision and actual request options, tests create/update/load without manual Run, reads complete monitor state and requires a final matching successful request. The criterion at functional/judge.toml:469 names the observable side-effect outcome rather than claiming universal non-evaluation proof. It distinguishes browser requests and keeps source fidelity separately scored. Public security.md:11 retains the absolute no-server-evaluation promise.
positive_observations.limitation: A working browser write does not establish every execution environment's network capability. The canary is distinguishing evidence for an important violation class, not universal assurance.

residual_limits.disposition: Explicit assurance limitation, not an instruction to weaken the public requirement
residual_limits.evidence: A server can evaluate source inside a context where fetch is unavailable and swallow the resulting error while storing exact text. This violates security.md:11 but produces the same browser observations as text-only storage. The repaired prompt and criterion correctly disclose this finite-canary limit.
residual_limits.recommendation: Keep a coverage/assurance record stating which observable violation class is exercised. Do not claim that a passing canary proves all server evaluation absent or add private-source/hidden-realm grading.

residual_limits.evidence: functional/prompt.md:402 requests a fresh monitor read after each operation but prescribes no settling interval before line 403 intentionally performs the same monitor update. A fire-and-forget server fetch may still be pending; the positive control can advance the revision and make a late canary request stale. No such race was executed here.
residual_limits.recommendation: Use a stated broad bounded observation window before the final positive write, informed by the successful control's response/readback latency and a scheduling margin; record its limit rather than claiming unbounded detection.
